Citation: Alberdi R., Fernandez E., Albizu I., Bedialauneta M.T., Fernandez R. IJEPES 133 (2021) 107305
Data / line: 30 kV distribution line, ACSR 147-AL1/34-ST1A (LA-180), complex terrain, Basque Country (Iberdrola); MACT 75 C; one measurement point (ultrasonic anemometer, air temp, solar); 1-min data ~3 yr; HIRLAM 0.05 deg NWP (AEMET), 6-hourly runs to 36 h, 3-h resolution; train 1 yr / test 2 yr; 10-min ampacity series
Forecast method: Linear-regression error reduction of NWP-based ampacity point forecast, then quantiles of observations conditional on point-forecast bins (10 A), linear in point forecast per quantile and horizon; non-parametric
Rule for setting the rating: Operator selects quantile tau (0.5-10 % evaluated); risk-vs-quantile curves (Figs 10-11) support the choice
Risk quantity controlled: tau = P(forecast > observed ampacity), Eq. (1); equated to MACT exceedance frequency when line carries forecast ampacity, Eq. (4); CIGRE TB 299 99 % criterion cited
Exceedance duration: Post-hoc: 90 % of excursions >10 min lasted <=20 min (1 % quantile) and <=30 min (10 % quantile); not part of the rule
Verification metrics: Reliability (% forecasts above observation) and PIT as observed/nominal %; normalised sharpness (mean distance to median / obs. 0.5-50 % spread); QS per quantile; median forecast ratio 100*forecast/obs for utilisation; probabilistic static rating as reference
Key numbers: PIT 98.8-99.7 % at 1 % quantile, 104-105 % at 0.5 %; static rating exceeded observed ampacity 11.6 % of time; utilisation falls with horizon
Use in review: S4 precedent (lower-tail evaluation, CRPS critique, forecast ratio, static-rating risk); S3 fixed-tau family; S4.4 excursion durations

Citation: Alberdi R., Albizu I., Fernandez E., Fernandez R., Bedialauneta M.T. IEEE TPWRD 37(1):329-337, 2022
Data / line: Same pilot line as Alberdi2021 (30 kV, LA-180 ACSR, Basque Country, MACT 75 C); cup + ultrasonic anemometers on one support; HIRLAM 0.05 deg with 4 h availability delay respected; train 1 yr / test 2 yr; 10-min series
Forecast method: Point forecasts by ARIMA (measurements only), linear regression and single-layer perceptron (measurements + NWP); probabilistic forecasts by subtracting unconditional training-error quantiles (assumed constant over time)
Rule for setting the rating: Operator selects low quantile tau (0.5-2.5 % shown most reliable)
Risk quantity controlled: tau = P(forecast > observed ampacity), Eq. (3); equated with MACT exceedance; CIGRE TB 299 criteria quoted: section avg temp not > MACT more than 1 % of time nor by 10 C; local temp never > MACT by 20 C
Verification metrics: Reliability diagram (observed vs nominal exceedance) for low quantiles; normalised sharpness Eq. (4); NMAE, NBias, NRMSE for point forecasts; critique of CRPS (equal weight, in amperes)
Key numbers: Static rating 482.3 A (0.6 m/s PE wind, 26 C, 1000 W/m2) exceeded MACT 11.6 % of time and violated 20 C local cap; raw NWP ampacity exceeded observations 78 %; point forecasts 50-55 %; NMAE ~10 % (1-2 h), <15 % longer
Use in review: S4.1 TB 299 criteria (frequency AND magnitude); S4.7 static-rating risk (primary source); S2 point-forecast exceedance ~50 %; S3 fixed-tau family; precursor of Alberdi2021 (unconditional vs conditional quantiles)

Citation: Molinar G., Gundlach J., Stork W. ISGT Latin America 2021, doi 10.1109/ISGTLatinAmerica52371.2021.9543043
Data / line: PrognoNetz benchmark (open, github.com/prognonetz/benchmark_idaho): INL Mesonet, Idaho, 2009-2014; virtual line between stations 690 and CIT; main + 4 auxiliary stations
Forecast method: CatBoost gradient boosting; (a) median model + per-horizon constant bias from training-error 2 % quantile; (b) model trained with 0.02 quantile loss
Rule for setting the rating: Fixed safety factor: 2 % overestimation rate (0.02 quantile); 1 % mentioned as alternative
Thermal model: Steady-state ampacity labels (model not detailed in this paper)
Verification metrics: Overestimation proportion on test set; error distributions; mean of negative errors (magnitude); quantile loss; MAPE by horizon
Key numbers: Bias model: 2 % target on training -> ~2.5 % on test; mean overestimation -112.5 A (bias) vs -50.7 A (0.02-GBR) at similar frequency; QLOSS 23x larger for bias model; achieved test rate for 0.02-GBR not reported; bias ~ -475 A at 1 h, ~ -650 A from 11 h
Use in review: S4.1 vocabulary (safety factor; TSO claim UNSOURCED, cites only Nguyen et al. CIRED 2014 for percentile-based safety factors); S4.6 in-sample target not out-of-sample guarantee; checklist magnitude row; S6 public benchmark exists (PrognoNetz)

Citation: Kirilenko A., Esmaili M., Chung C.Y. IEEE TPWRS 36(4):3070-3079, 2021 (U. Saskatchewan; NSERC + SaskPower funding)
Data / line: Hourly weather, Assiniboia Airport (Saskatchewan), interpolated to 5 min; train June-July 2019, test August 2019 (744 hourly OPFs at 5-min resolution); RTS test system, 60 km line, ACSR Falcon, Tmax 80 C; SLR 1269 A (35 C, 0.6 m/s, 900 W/m2)
Forecast method: Linear quantile regression and superquantile (CVaR) regression of conductor temperature on lagged current, current^2, weather and bilinear terms (k = 1-3 lags)
Rule for setting the rating: Constraint: alpha-quantile or upper-tail superquantile of conductor temperature <= Tmax, embedded in multi-period AC OPF; closed-form max current for k = 1
Risk quantity controlled: Risk on conductor TEMPERATURE (not rating), nominal 5 %; superquantile bounds expected tail temperature
Thermal model: Transient, via time-lagged regression (data-driven dynamics); validated with transient HBE
Exceedance duration: Implicit via thermal dynamics; notes small overheating smoothed by inertia
Verification metrics: Actual risk = fraction of intervals with T > Tmax after re-simulation with realised weather; average excess temperature; transferred energy; Pareto front
Regime conditioning: None (sensitivity to forecast error SD via variance scaling)
Key numbers: Actual risk: CC 0.81 %, QR1 1.44 %, QR3 1.85 %, SQR1 0.73 %, SQR2 0.87 %, LS 6.29 %; avg excess temp 83.9-90.5 C; QR2 +31.7 % energy vs SLR
Use in review: S3 temperature-based + CVaR family (only SQR application); S4.1 rating vs temperature vs realised risk distinction (nominal 5 % -> realised 0.7-1.9 %); S4 short evaluation period; Canadian work

Citation: Dupin R., Michiorri A., Kariniotakis G. CIRED Workshop, Helsinki, 2016, paper 347, doi 10.1049/cp.2016.0722
Data / line: Virtual France-Belgium line, single point; Lynx 175 mm2; ECMWF reanalysis every 12 h as "observations" (solar set to 0); ECMWF NWP at 4 nearby points; EPEX/BELPEX spot, RTE/Elia balancing costs; train 2014, test 2015
Rule for setting the rating: Newsvendor optimal quantile tau* = pi+/(pi+ + pi-): pi+ = spot price difference (lost benefit), pi- = sum of imbalance costs; fixed arbitrary vs dynamic monthly/hourly
Risk quantity controlled: tau = P(forecast > observation); chosen for expected financial cost only, NO safety cost included
Verification metrics: MAPE (QRF 8.1 % vs persistence 11.4 %); financial benefit normalised to 1 % quantile
Key numbers: States that most works arbitrarily pick 1 %; best fixed tau 14 % (+15.1 % benefit vs 1 %); mean dynamic tau 7.5-8.2 %, monthly range 2.1-18.2 %; 50 % quantile gives 76.7 % of 1 % benefit; text says benefits "during 2016" although test year is 2015 (inconsistency)
Use in review: S3 economic (newsvendor) family; tension: economic optimum (~8-14 %) vs safety convention (1 %) because safety cost omitted -> argue for constrained rule tau = min(tau*, alpha_max)

Citation: Dupin R., Michiorri A., Kariniotakis G. IEEE TPWRS 34(4):2836-2848, 2019
Data / line: UK line, 6 weather stations, 5-min data 2009-2010; ECMWF NWP 0.125 deg; each station treated as if critical span; IEEE 24-bus with 2 DLR lines; ENTSO-E 2010 FR/DE load bootstrap; seasonal SLR set below observed DLR 99 % of time
Forecast method: QRF (2000 trees), 999 quantiles 0.1-99.9 %; monthly sliding retraining
Rule for setting the rating: Fixed tau (1 %, 20 %), risk-neutral two-stage/bilevel stochastic SCOPF, and risk-averse bilevel with risk appetite function v_beta (linear, quadratic, exponential) on reserve activation costs; lookup tables
Risk quantity controlled: tau on rating; risk proxied by reserve activation cost and frequency of incidents (cost > 1500 EUR)
Exceedance duration: Not addressed (preventive N-1, no corrective penalties)
Verification metrics: MAPE (11.1 % vs persistence 16.1 %); reliability at 0.1/1/2 %; benefit vs reserve cost and incident frequency curves
Formal tests: YES: binomial 99 % bounds (0.14/1.11/2.16 %) vs observed 0.8/1.8/2.7 % -> forecasts declared unreliable; assumes independence of ~45,000 correlated forecasts (24 horizons x 6 stations)
Key numbers: Benefits 0.61 % (tau 1 %), 0.97 % (tau 20 %), 1.01 % risk-neutral; 7x reserve charges and incidents vs 1 %; risk-averse strategies up to ~20 % more benefit at low cost; lists fixed tau in literature: NETFLEX 2 % (Nguyen 2013/2014), 1/5/10/20 % (Hoekstra 2012), 1 % (Ringelband 2013), 10 % (Aznarte), 2.5 % (Nexans at FERC)
Use in review: S3 stochastic/risk-averse family; S4.3 only formal coverage test (credit + independence critique); S4.1 source of 2 % (NETFLEX) and SLR 99 % convention; reliability-vs-value debate (S4.7)

Citation: Dupin R., Cavalcante L., Bessa R.J., Kariniotakis G., Michiorri A. Energies 13(12):3090, 2020
Data / line: Same UK data and IEEE 24-bus test case as Dupin2019; DLR capped at 125 % of SLR
Forecast method: QRF with lower tail (<5 %) replaced by exponential distribution; shape parameter per k-means cluster of (5 %, 10 %) quantile forecasts; horizons grouped in blocks of 6
Rule for setting the rating: Fixed tau and risk-averse bilevel strategy (as Dupin2019)
Verification metrics: Relative overestimation frequency at 1 % and 0.1 %; sharpness; QSS restricted to 0.1-5 % (proposed); benefit vs reserve cost / incident frequency
Formal tests: None in this paper; notes ~110 observations below 5 % quantile per horizon block (~10 per cluster)
Regime conditioning: Tail shape conditioned on forecast-distribution clusters (not reported as conditional coverage)
Key numbers: Relative frequency 180 -> 100 % at 1 %, 800 -> 200 % at 0.1 % (328 -> 191 % with 4 vs 1 cluster); 1 % quantile ~20 A lower; fixed 1 %: reserve cost -37 % but benefit -25 %; at equal benefit incidents +18-35 % (fixed tau) but -29-35 % with risk-averse strategies; claims CRPS/Brier lose relevance; QSS differences <0.01 % can hide large value differences
Use in review: S4.2 first CRPS critique + lower-tail QSS; S4.3 small tail samples; S4.7 reliability vs value; S3 coupling between forecast tail quality and decision strategy

Citation: Safari N., Mazhari S.M., Chung C.Y., Ko S.B. JMPCE 10(2):378-387, 2022 (U. Saskatchewan / SaskPower; NSERC + SaskPower)
Data / line: NREL M2 met tower (public), 2010-2015; analysis on 2010-2011, 85 % train/validation, 15 % test (~2600 h); hypothetical Drake 26/7 ACSR at 1861 m; STLR for 0.6 m/s, 40 C, 1000 W/m2; measurement-only, no NWP
Forecast method: mRMR feature selection incl. latent variables (convective and radiative heat terms); LSTM-based stacked denoising autoencoder + 3 LSTM models; fine-tuned with quantile-type "secure" cost function
Rule for setting the rating: Fixed POE* (90, 95, 99 %) chosen by operator; notes optimal POE could come from risk/annealing cost assessment
Risk quantity controlled: POE = P(actual >= forecast) = 1 - alpha; cites CIGRE TB 299 (Seppa & Salehian, called "IEEE/CIGRE JTF") for 99 % criterion
Thermal model: Steady-state IEEE 738-2012; transients explicitly ignored (steady state reached within ~30 min)
Verification metrics: Achieved POE, NMAE, RMSE; histograms of predicted DTLR
Key numbers: Achieved POE at targets 90/95/99: proposed 91.90/95.14/99.01; QR 92.20/96.60/99.80; QRF 92.64/95.56/99.31; persistence 83.42/89.57/95.75; latent variables cut NMAE 19.21->18.51 % at POE 99
Use in review: S4.1 POE vocabulary; S4.3 one-sided vs two-sided (QR at 99.8 % = ~5 exceedances vs 26 expected, rejected by Kupiec); S4.6 secure loss; S6 public dataset (NREL M2); Canadian work

Citation: Lawal O.A., Teh J. IEEE Access 10:65193-65205, 2022
Data / line: UK 100 km line, 2 weather stations 50 km apart; hourly data for 30 days (720 h); IEEE 738; STR 3305 A
Forecast method: QR (25/50/75th percentiles), ensemble means (Monte Carlo), RNN, CNN
Rule for setting the rating: Recommends 50th percentile QR as "more conservative, secure"
Risk quantity controlled: Percentile defined conventionally ("75th percentile is the value below which 75 % of observations may be found"); security judged against MAXIMUM line ampacity over period
Verification metrics: MAE, MAPE, RMSE, RAE, rMAE, rRMSE; skill; CRPS; PICP; Brier score (all 0.000); PIAW; PBP = share of hours actual > forecast
Key numbers: PBP (Table 3, multiples of 1/24): 25 % QR 16.67, 50 % QR 33.33, 75 % QR 91.70, ensemble/RNN/CNN 79.17 -> 50th percentile forecast above actual in ~67 % of hours
Use in review: S4.1 example (conventional percentile, nominal alpha 0.5); S4.3 single-day evaluation; S1 prior survey (methods-focused); treat neutrally

Citation: Lawal O.A., Teh J. Electric Power Systems Research 214 (2023) 108807
Data / line: UK line, weather stations hourly "for several days"; IEEE 738; SLR 2430 A
Horizons: 12, 24, 48 h; evaluation over one 48 h period (N = 48)
Rule for setting the rating: Recommends 75th percentile QR and ensemble forecasting as most reliable
Risk quantity controlled: Percentile conventional ("60th percentile is the value below which 60 % of all observations occur"); "a conservative forecast rating is expected not to surpass the maximum DLR"
Verification metrics: Point errors; skill; PICP; Brier score; PIAW; PBP = COUNT(actual > forecast)/N
Key numbers: 75th percentile QR PBP 68.8 % (= 33/48) -> forecast above actual ~31 % of hours; ensemble PBP 75 %; skill 97-99 %
Use in review: S4.1 motivating example (verified: conventional percentile; achieved alpha ~0.31 on 48 h); S4.3 evaluation too short; neutral wording; 50 Scopus citations

Citation: Fan F., Bell K., Infield D. IEEE Trans. Power Del. 32(4):1881-1890, 2017, doi 10.1109/TPWRD.2016.2577140 (Strathclyde; SPEN/NGET funding)
Data / line: 90 km 132 kV double-circuit OHL, North Wales (SPEN); 9 weather stations; 10-min data, 108 winter days (14/12/2012-31/03/2013); spans CQ34-CQ35 (Lynx ACSR 175) and AC102-AC101B (Poplar AAAC 200); winter SLR 485 A / 607 A
Forecast method: AR/VAR with Fourier de-trending; normal / truncated normal / von Mises predictive distributions; conditionally heteroscedastic spread; min-CRPS estimation; Monte Carlo through thermal model; KDE for rating percentiles
Rule for setting the rating: Fixed percentile (P1, P5, P10); P5 proposed as "The Limit"; 125 % SLR practical cap discussed
Verification metrics: PIT histograms of RTTR forecasts; CPI widths; RMSE by rating level; additional capacity above SLR; share of time percentiles exceed SLR
Regime conditioning: By forecast rating level (P5 < 125 % SLR vs >= 125 % SLR)
Key numbers: P5 3-step exceedance 3.68 % (n=6662) vs 5.02 % (n=2410) at CQ34-CQ35; 3.02 % (n=4207) vs 5.32 % (n=4865) at AC102-AC101B; single miss 262.6 A vs SLR 607 A after forecast wind >3 m/s realised 1.3 m/s with 45 deg direction change; 125 % cap too high in 3 % / 2.1 % of cases
Use in review: S3 fixed-percentile family; S4.1 alpha vocabulary; S4.2 CRPS/PIT practice; S4.5 only published regime split (by forecast rating level)

Citation: Molinar G., Fan L.T., Stork W. IEEE ISGT 2019, doi 10.1109/ISGT.2019.8791615
Data / line: INL Mesonet (Idaho), simulated 49 km line through CIT station; Drake ACSR, MACT 100 C; hourly data; train summer 2014, test summer 2015
Forecast method: Quantile regression forest from past 20 h of local + auxiliary station measurements (no NWP); PCA-rotated wind vectors
Verification metrics: MAE, MAPE only (despite QRF being probabilistic)
Key numbers: 24 h MAPE 19.56 % (MAE 265 A); 48 h MAPE 16.61 % -> 15.91 % with PCA rotation; cites Twenties/FlexNet report: max 20 % MAPE acceptable to most European TSOs
Use in review: S4.2 example of probabilistic method verified only by point metrics; S5 TSO acceptance criterion stated as MAPE (point accuracy), not risk; precursor of PrognoNetz benchmark

Citation: Teng F., Dupin R., Michiorri A., Kariniotakis G., Chen Y., Strbac G. IEEE TPWRS 33(3):3306-3314, 2018
Data / line: Forecasts: QRF on southern Sweden 2010 hourly weather + ECMWF NWP to 48 h; system studies on 2-bus and modified IEEE 24-bus (27,702 scenarios filtered)
Forecast method: QRF ampacity forecasts discretised into 9 rating scenarios (1.0-1.8 x SLR in illustrative table)
Rule for setting the rating: Risk-neutral two-stage stochastic UC co-optimising energy, reserve, re-dispatch with DLR, wind and outage scenarios; compares SLR, real-time-only DLR, single optimal rating, fully optimised
Risk quantity controlled: Expected cost; Eq. (6) defines tau = P(forecast > observation) but full distribution used
Verification metrics: Operating cost, wind curtailment; no forecast verification reported
Regime conditioning: Correlation between wind and DLR examined
Key numbers: 2-bus: SLR 42.3 kGBP, real-time only 35.1, best single rating (1.15 x SLR) 34.5, fully optimised 32.3; curtailment 525 -> 316 MWh; scenarios exclude ratings below SLR
Use in review: S3 stochastic family (risk-neutral; safety via real-time correction; scenario truncation at SLR); S5 role of monitoring

Citation: McJunkin et al., IEEE Trans. Power Del. 40(2):739-749, 2025 (Idaho National Laboratory)
Data / line: Two 69/138 kV lines, Long Island NY (NYISO), offshore-wind integration; assumed SLR 925 A; 72 MesoWest stations; 2020 only
Horizons: Hour-ahead (HRRR hourly, 15-min, 18 h) and day-ahead (36 h runs 4x/day)
Forecast method: Deterministic: HRRR weather into INL GLASS span-level DLR; line rating = min over spans
Rule for setting the rating: Deterministic derating: min(previous, current hour-ahead forecast) - I_d, I_d = 0-140 A; cap 130% SLR (load-dump limit); floor I_m (no wind, full sun, 40 C)
Risk quantity controlled: Operational risk = frequency and magnitude of misses (forecast > real-time DLR), i.e. last-minute downgrades; operational benefit = mean rating increase
Thermal model: IEEE 738 via GLASS (steady state, all spans)
Exceedance duration: Not modelled; misses counted per hour
Verification metrics: Back-test histograms of miss magnitude; mean benefit/risk curves vs I_d; notes mean miss diluted by no-miss hours
Regime conditioning: None explicit; line geometry (N-S vs E-W) discussed
Key numbers: 120 A derating: misses >180 A cut to 15-16/yr; mean gain ~65 A and ~25 A. 60 A misses ~1/day needs ~120 A derate HA (gain ~150 A, 16%) or ~80 A DA (gain ~90 A, 10%). DLR uncertainty ~50% smaller contribution to wind-delivery risk than wind-power forecast error. Mentions FERC Order 881 (intro only).
Use in review: Sec 3 deterministic-margin family (anchor); Sec 4 magnitude/frequency back-test; Sec 6 regulatory: only paper mentioning Order 881; operator-centric risk; 130% cap

Citation: Rashkovska, Jancic, Depolli, Kosmac, Kosec, IEEE Trans. Power Syst. 37(6):4642-4650, 2022 (ELES, Slovenia)
Data / line: Two lines (Obersielach-Podlog; Cerkno-Idrija), weather stations at 5-min, 2019-2020; conductor surface temperature; ELES network 29 lines, >2000 spans
Horizons: Nowcast; short-term 0-12 h; medium-term 12-72 h (Aladin-derived NWP)
Forecast method: Monte Carlo through DiTeR (extended CIGRE) using location-fitted Epanechnikov kernel weather-error PDFs; pre-computed database of 972 normalised ampacity CDFs (3 horizons x 6 wind speeds x 3 directions x 6 conductors x 3 emissivities), homotopy interpolation
Rule for setting the rating: Lower/upper limits of a central interval at user-selected confidence level p (source writes CDF = p/2 and 1 - p/2; read as (1-p)/2 and (1+p)/2)
Verification metrics: KS tests of normality (rejected, p<1e-4) and horizon equality of weather errors; DTR model error from surface temperature vs weather-driven error
Formal tests: No coverage back-test of issued interval
Regime conditioning: Wind speed/direction and conductor type/emissivity drive distribution shape; low-wind regime asymmetric (wind error centred ~+1 m/s; nominal rating in lower tail; zero-wind rating = minimum)
Key numbers: Weather error dominates model error even for nowcast; at 99% confidence lower limit < static 645 A (243-AL1/39) 5.21% of time; operational at ELES since Aug 2020; real-time every 1 min, forecasts every 5 min; lookup tens-hundreds ms
Use in review: Sec 4 reference-ampacity (model vs weather error), regime asymmetry; Sec 6 European TSO operational practice; static rating not risk-free

Citation: Aznarte & Siebert, IEEE Trans. Power Del. 32(1):335-343, 2017 (NIE, Northern Ireland)
Data / line: Two 110 kV lines Omagh-Dungannon (~10 km each), 10 reference poles, 5-min measurements; Lynx partly replaced by INVAR; ~50/50 train/test split at 2010-01-01
Horizons: Up to 27 h ahead at 15-min resolution
Forecast method: GLM, MARS, RF, QRF with ECMWF deterministic NWP (00/12 UTC, 3-h step, 0.25 deg grid, downscaled) + lagged ratings and weather (29 inputs); persistence and downscaled-NWP baselines
Rule for setting the rating: 10% quantile (QRF) minus a safety margin = max shortfall of that quantile vs computed rating over previous 6 months (called very conservative); suggests weather-dependent margins
Thermal model: NIE-adapted CIGRE; reference = computed rating from measured pole weather
Verification metrics: NMAE (Twenties KPI <35%), normalised bias; reliability diagram (1-3 h) ; sharpness (inter-quantile ranges 40/60/80%)
Regime conditioning: Pole A3 outlier traced to irradiance sensor shading
Key numbers: MARS/RF ~14-15% NMAE at long horizons; persistence best only in first hour; QRF reliability 'satisfactory', slightly over-predicts low quantiles (conservative) - no numbers in text; earlier second-hand figures (5% at 10%, 11-12% at 20%) NOT verifiable from text
Use in review: Sec 3 margin family (probabilistic variant); Sec 4 reliability claim corrected to qualitative; reference = computed rating
